title: Horizon and Archive
premise: Ines Lockridge, a terraformer tending a garden meant for colonists not yet born, runs supply routes between two worlds that severed contact decades ago. When the name of her dead brother appears on the manifest of a ship that never flew, she discovers that an entire colony's massacre has been erased from every archive — and that the erasure is still being enforced. To prove it happened, Ines must recover the one uncorrupted record hidden inside the terraforming reactor itself, racing its scheduled shutdown countdown while the archivists who rewrote history hunt her across both worlds. She succeeds at terrible cost: the truth goes public, justice arrives outside any courtroom, and Ines plants the garden's first seed in soil finally honest about what it grew from.
about_author: Ansel Fairweather is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote survey stations before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about people who maintain things — gardens, ships, records — and what those maintenance routines conceal.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ines Lockridge pilots a supply run between Meridian and Cael Harbor, two colonies that stopped speaking after 'the Severance.' Her POV establishes her solitary routine tending the Foundling Garden, seeded for future generations. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness interrupted by wonder when she finds an anomaly: a manifest entry bearing her brother Tomas's name on a ship decommissioned before his birth.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Ines investigates the manifest in the orbital archive, discovering the vessel Halcyon listed as destroyed with all hands — yet its flight logs continue for eleven years after. Switching to the perspective of Archivist Corvin Ashe, we see him flagging her query as a breach. The beat shifts from curiosity to dread: someone is watching her search in real time.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines returns to Meridian and interrogates the garden's own sensor archives, finding soil chemistry consistent with mass burning forty years ago — the era of the Severance. Old gardener Sefa Ilo reveals fragments of a suppressed event called the Kettlefield action. POV alternates between Ines and Sefa; the beat is grief surfacing through physical evidence the archive cannot fully erase.

chapters.title: The Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: The terraforming reactor, which powers the archive vaults, enters its planned end-of-life shutdown sequence — ninety days until all deep storage goes cold forever. Corvin Ashe, now POV, realizes the truth may be buried in the reactor's shielded physical core, beyond digital reach. The beat is a ticking clock established on both sides: hunter and hunted now share one deadline.

chapters.title: Cael Harbor Silence
chapters.summary: Ines risks the forbidden crossing to Cael Harbor, seeking survivors' descendants. She meets Ryn Oduya, whose grandmother died at Kettlefield but whose family name was reassigned to living collaborators. Through Ryn's eyes we feel the wound of complicity; the beat is bitter kinship — two people discovering they were raised on opposite sides of the same lie.

chapters.title: The Rewriting
chapters.summary: Corvin's chapter reveals the machinery of erasure: he was trained by the original archivists who converted massacre records into 'administrative noise,' and he has spent his career maintaining the lie out of institutional loyalty rather than malice. When his superiors order Ines's route sabotaged, Corvin hesitates. The beat is corruption shown as procedure — evil as paperwork done faithfully.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: With the reactor at nineteen days, Ines and Ryn infiltrate the vault access corridors, guided by Sefa's stolen credentials. A betrayal by a Cael contact traps them in a flooding coolant gallery; Ines nearly drowns saving the recovered data shard. POV stays close with Ines throughout. The beat is terror and sacrifice — the cost of proof made bodily.

chapters.title: The Core
chapters.summary: Corvin, shaken by the sabotage order, defects and meets Ines at the reactor's inner core, where the original unredacted archive survives on analog crystal. He confesses his role in maintaining the lie. As they extract the record, security forces breach the facility. The beat is uneasy alliance and moral reckoning — the gatekeeper opening the gate at last.

chapters.title: Kettlefield, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Climax: cornered in the failing reactor, Ines broadcasts the raw Kettlefield records on every open channel as the shutdown completes, choosing truth over escape. Corvin holds the corridor and is killed; Ryn pulls Ines out through the coolant vents. The beat is catharsis through exposure — the massacre named publicly, irrevocably, at the price of a life.

chapters.title: First Seed
chapters.summary: Resolution: months later, tribunals convened outside official law try the surviving archivists, while both colonies reopen dialogue over the shared grief. Ines, cleared but changed, plants the Foundling Garden's first seed in soil tested against the true record. Final image: the manifest restored, Tomas's name among the honored dead. The beat is hard-won peace — memory reestablished as the ground everything grows from.
